articles.title: Veja como foi o debate com os candidatos ao governo do Maranhão na TV Mirante
articles.summary: Participam os candidatos André Luís (Missão), Eduardo Braide (PSD), Felipe Camarão (PT), Orleans Brandão (MDB), Roberto Rocha (PRTB) e Saulo Arcangeli (PSTU). Debate foi realizado na terça-feira (29) e foi mediado pelo jornalista Hélter Duarte, da TV Globo.
articles.body:
Participam os candidatos André Luís (Missão), Eduardo Braide (PSD), Felipe Camarão (PT), Orleans Brandão (MDB), Roberto Rocha (PRTB) e Saulo Arcangeli (PSTU). Debate foi realizado na terça-feira (29) e foi mediado pelo jornalista Hélter Duarte, da TV Globo.

Debate foi realizado na terça-feira (29) e foi mediado pelo jornalista Hélter Duarte, da TV Globo.

Participaram os candidatos André Luís (Missão), Eduardo Braide (PSD), Felipe Camarão (PT), Orleans Brandão (MDB), Roberto Rocha (PRTB) e Saulo Arcangeli (PSTU).

Encontro teve mais de duas horas de duração com quatro blocos, sendo dois de tema livre e dois de tema determinado, além das considerações finais.

O g1 agradece a audiência durante o debate entre os candidatos ao governo do Maranhão. Até a próxima cobertura!

Fim do debate entre os candidatos ao governo do Maranhão.

O sexto candidato a fazer suas considerações finais é Orleans Brandão (MDB).

O quinto candidato a fazer suas considerações finais é André Luís (Missão).

O quarto candidato a fazer suas considerações finais é Felipe Camarão (PT).

O terceiro candidato a fazer suas considerações finais é Roberto Rocha (PRTB).

O segundo candidato a fazer suas considerações finais é Eduardo Braide (PSD).

Começam as considerações finais. O primeiro candidato a falar é Saulo Arcangeli (PSTU). A ordem foi definida em sorteio.

Início do quarto e último bloco do debate.

Começa o debate com os candidatos ao governo do Maranhão na TV Mirante. Acompanhe!

Tudo pronto para começar o debate com candidatos ao governo do Maranhão.

Em entrevista, o candidato Eduardo Braide (PSD) falou sobre a expectativa para o debate e afirmou que o encontro será uma oportunidade para que os candidatos apresentem suas propostas. Ele também destacou temas como segurança pública e saúde como prioridades para o Maranhão.

"Uma expectativa que eu acho que é de todo o Maranhão poder acompanhar as propostas de cada candidato, o que pensa cada um, o que já fez cada um. Eu tenho certeza que será uma grande noite da democracia. Acho que as propostas é o que deve prevalecer hoje, para que o povo do Maranhão possa avaliar aquele que está mais preparado, que tem mais condições de cuidar da vida de 7 milhões de maranhenses a partir do ano que vem. E, sem sombra de dúvidas, segurança, saúde, algo que qualquer maranhense clama pela discussão desses dois temas. Eu tenho certeza que serão dois temas abordados no debate de hoje", diz o candidato.

O candidato Eduardo Braide (PSD) foi o último a chegar aos estúdios da TV Mirante para o debate com candidatos ao governo do Maranhão.

articles.title: Debate pelo governo do TO chega ao fim; veja os destaques
articles.summary: Participam do debate Laurez Moreira (PSD), Professor Witer Naves (PSOL), Professora Dorinha (União) e Vicentinho Júnior (PSDB).
articles.body:
Participam do debate Laurez Moreira (PSD), Professor Witer Naves (PSOL), Professora Dorinha (União) e Vicentinho Júnior (PSDB).

Debate ocorreu nesta terça-feira (29), depois da novela Quem Ama Cuida, da TV Globo.

Programa foi dividido em quatro blocos com temas livres e determinados por sorteio, além de um bloco destinado às considerações finais.

No primeiro e no terceiro blocos, os candidatos poderão abordar temas livres.

No segundo e no quarto, as perguntas serão sobre temas definidos pela produção e sorteados ao vivo.

Encerrado o debate realizado pela TV Anhanguera com os candidatos ao governo do Tocantins. Reveja os vídeos do programa.

Vicentinho Júnior (PSDB) encerra a rodada de considerações.

Agora é a vez da Professora Dorinha (União) fazer sua conclusão.

Laurez Moreira (PSD) faz suas considerações finais.

Candidatos iniciam as considerações finais. A ordem também foi definida em sorteio. O primeiro é o Professor Witer Naves (PSOL).

Quarto bloco finalizado. Em instantes, candidatos farão suas considerações finais.

Chegamos agora ao último bloco do programa. As perguntas serão sobre temas definidos pela produção e sorteados ao vivo. Cada candidato terá direito a fazer uma pergunta e a responder uma vez. Ao final, cada um terá um tempo reservado para fazer suas considerações finais.

Começa o terceiro bloco do debate. Assim como no primeiro, os candidatos poderão abordar temas livres. Cada candidato terá direito a fazer uma pergunta e a responder uma vez.

Fim do segundo bloco. Voltamos em instantes.

Começa o segundo bloco. Neste momento, as perguntas serão sobre temas definidos pela produção e sorteados ao vivo. Cada candidato terá direito a fazer uma pergunta e a responder uma vez.

Fim do primeiro bloco. Voltamos em instantes.

Começa o debate. Neste primeiro bloco, os candidatos poderão abordar temas livres. A ordem das perguntas foi definida em sorteio. Em todos os blocos, cada candidato terá direito a fazer uma pergunta e a responder uma vez.

Vicentinho Júnior explicou o que espera do debate.

"Hoje é o último debate do primeiro turno. Então é como eu tenho dito durante todos os outros debates que fizemos, as oportunidades que nos foram dadas, eu vou tratar esse momento eleitoral com muito respeito, vou aproveitar esse momento rico de um horário nobre pra mim me apresentar mais uma vez, apresentar as nossas propostas que até aqui nos trouxe a caminhada do 45. Continuarei a respeitar as pessoas, a respeitar a matéria humana e tô pronto pra um bom debate, a como me for chamado. Então, o tocantinense conhece o jeito do Vicentinho Júnior de ser, um homem respeitoso, um homem cauteloso, mas um homem que sempre fez o bom enfrentamento quando necessário foi. Então, hoje, em um último programa, eu não posso ser diferente disso, a não ser um candidato que quer mostrar ao povo tocantinense que a verdadeira mudança é que faz bem".

Laurez também falou sobre sua expectativa para o debate.

"A expectativa é muito boa. Eu sempre tenho o maior prazer de fazer com que as pessoas me conheçam o máximo. Porque quem conhece a história de Laurez Moreira, o seu passado, o legado que eu tenho deixado por onde eu tenho passado, sempre me apoia, né? Eu tenho certeza de que eu quero que o povo do estado do Tocantins, todos me conheçam e conheçam bem a minha essência como homem, como pai de família, como político e a pessoa que sempre tá na política por vocação e por vontade de servir a nossa gente. Eu espero que as pessoas possam fazer uma avaliação melhor de todos os candidatos, para conhecer o perfil, o que que pensa, a maneira de agir de cada um".

Professora Dorinha (União Brasil) falou de sua expectativa para o debate.

"Eu acho que é uma oportunidade que a imprensa tanto dá para o candidato, no meu caso, a candidata, falar sobre as propostas, projetos, como enxerga, é, o estado, quanto para o eleitor avaliar e comparar candidatos, comparar propostas. É, eu acho que, dentro da estrutura democrática do nosso país, a imprensa cumpre um papel extremamente importante. Então, é um debate muito esperado durante a campanha toda, né? E a minha expectativa é que a gente possa discutir projeto, ideia, modelo do estado."

Witer Naves (PSOL) falou sobre a expectativa para o debate.

"Tem uma importância histórica do campo democrático, e a gente acredita que esse debate hoje, ele constrói, sem dúvida alguma, alguns marcos para o domingo. Então, domingo a gente tem a aquilo que a gente ao longo de todo o processo está construindo, mas que sem dúvida alguma, a TV Globo, a sua afiliada TV Anhanguera ajudou na história do Brasil a construir, que foi a tomada de decisão significativamente, a tomada de decisão do eleitor aqui do Tocantins e do Brasil".

O debate será dividido em quatro blocos, com perguntas feitas entre os próprios candidatos. Em todos os blocos, cada candidato terá direito a fazer uma pergunta e a responder uma vez. No primeiro e no terceiro blocos, os candidatos poderão abordar temas livres. Já no segundo e no quarto, as perguntas serão sobre temas definidos pela produção e sorteados ao vivo.

Os tempos serão os mesmos em todos os blocos. O candidato que fizer a pergunta terá 30 segundos para formulá-la e 1 minuto e 15 segundos para a réplica. Quem responder terá 3 minutos e 15 segundos, que poderão ser divididos entre a resposta e a tréplica.

A ordem das perguntas de cada bloco foi sorteada previamente, na presença de representantes dos candidatos. Ao final do quarto bloco, cada candidato terá um tempo reservado para fazer suas considerações finais.

Boa noite. A TV Anhanguera realiza nesta terça-feira (29) o debate com candidatos ao governo do Tocantins. O programa será exibido logo após a novela Quem Ama Cuida, da TV Globo. O g1 transmite ao vivo.

articles.title: Candidatos ao governo de MT participam de debate na TV Centro América; acompanhe ao vivo
articles.summary: Participam do debate os candidatos Dra. Natasha (PSD), Otaviano Pivetta (Republicanos) e Wellington Fagundes (PL).
articles.body:
Participam do debate os candidatos Dra. Natasha (PSD), Otaviano Pivetta (Republicanos) e Wellington Fagundes (PL).

Debate é realizado nesta terça-feira (29), nos estúdios da TV Centro América.

Foram convidados os candidatos cujos partidos tiveram representação de, no mínimo, cinco parlamentares eleitos no Congresso Nacional em 2022.

Programa é dividido em quatro blocos com temas livres e determinados por sorteio.

Termina o debate. Candidatos trocaram acusações e apresentaram propostas para saúde, violência contra mulher, administração pública, entre outros; leia mais aqui

Candidatos fazem as considerações finais.

Começa o quarto e último bloco do debate.

Candidatos ao governo de Mato Grosso já estão posicionados no estúdio da TV Centro América para o início do debate!

Otaviano Pivetta (Republicanos) foi o terceiro candidato a chegar para o debate. Ele afirmou que se sente preparado caso seja eleito.

"Minha expectativa é me comunicar com o povo de Mato Grosso, debater sobre ideias, sobre projetos. Represento um modelo de gestão que vem dando certo em Mato Grosso e o meu dever é fazer cada vez melhor. Um novo ciclo que se inicia em janeiro, me sinto preparado e pronto para isso. Vou pedir ao povo que confie em mim, que eu vou honrar a confiança".

Doutora Natasha (PSD) foi a segunda candidata a chegar para o debate. Ela disse que as expectativas são as melhores possíveis.

“A gente tem uma expectativa muito positiva, muito grande mesmo, tendo em vista que estamos virando em cima dos candidatos que se mostraram à frente o tempo todo da campanha. Então, é um momento muito importante, além de se apresentar, falar das nossas propostas e estar em contato com nossos eleitores".

O candidato Wellington Fagundes (PL) foi o primeiro a chegar. Para ele, o debate é uma oportunidade da população conhecer suas propostas.

"Que a democracia vença, a liberdade de cada um de ir e vir, que seja implantada neste país. E por isso nós acreditamos muito que esse debate é uma oportunidade para que toda a população saiba do governo Wellington Fagundes, um governo humano, para cuidar das pessoas que vivem, que constroem o nosso estado de Mato Grosso".

O debate com candidatos ao governo de Mato Grosso começa logo após a novela "Quem Ama Cuida", às 21h15. Confira as regras:

O debate terá quatro blocos . Em dois, as perguntas serão de tema livre; nos outros dois, os temas serão determinados.

As perguntas serão feitas de um candidato para outro. Todos terão oportunidade de perguntar e responder . A ordem de abertura de cada bloco foi definida por sorteio.

Em cada rodada, o candidato terá 30 segundos para fazer a pergunta . O candidato escolhido terá até 3 minutos e 30 segundos, divididos entre a resposta e a tréplica.

Quem fez a pergunta terá 1 minuto e 30 segundos para a réplica .

Ao fim do quarto bloco, cada candidato fará suas considerações finais .

A TV Centro América realiza o debate com os candidatos ao governo de Mato Grosso, na terça-feira (29), a partir das 22h15.Participarão do debate os candidatos Dra. Natasha (PSD), Otaviano Pivetta (Republicanos) e Wellington Fagundes (PL).

O mediador será o jornalista e apresentador Cleto Kipper. O g1 Mato Grosso vai transmitir ao vivo, acompanhe!

articles.summary: Candidato ao governo foi entrevistado pela TV Bahia nesta terça-feira (29). Inicialmente, estava previsto um debate com outros dois concorrentes, mas eles não compareceram.
articles.body:
O candidato ao governo da Bahia ACM Neto ( União Brasil ) foi entrevistado pela TV Bahia, nesta terça-feira (29). O programa foi transmitido ao vivo pela emissora e pelo g1 , com apresentação da jornalista Zileide Silva , da TV Globo. As perguntas foram sorteadas na hora.

A TV Bahia promoveria um debate entre os postulantes a chefe do Executivo baiano, mas Ronaldo Mansur ( PSOL ) não pôde participar, pois está hospitalizado após um acidente de carro , e Jerônimo Rodrigues ( PT ) cumpriu agenda externa de campanha e optou por não comparecer.

ACM Neto começou sua participação prestando solidariedade ao candidato Ronaldo Mansur e, em seguida fez críticas a Jerônimo Rodrigues, por faltar ao confronto de ideias com ele. As cobranças seguiram até o fim da entrevista, em temas distintos, como segurança pública, saúde e educação.

Questionado sobre segurança pública, ACM Neto falou sobre as medidas que espera implantar com a governadoria da segurança, um dos seus principais projetos de campanha para o setor.

ACM Neto em entrevista na TV Bahia — Foto: Alan Oliveira/g1

Com relação à educação, o candidato se comprometeu a proporcionar uma transformação da qualidade de ensino no estado. Também garantiu que, caso seja eleito, vai manter programas já implantados pelo governo atual, como o "Pé de Meia" e o "Bolsa Presença", que têm como objetivo garantir permanência, presença e a conclusão escolar de estudantes.

Disse ainda que quer proporcionar para os adolescentes e jovens uma educação que torne a escola mais atrativa para o aluno.

Em seguida, o candidato se comprometeu a governar a Bahia com qualquer que seja o presidente eleito pelo povo e ao lado dos prefeitos de cada uma das 417 cidades do estado, independentemente do seu partido.

Com relação à saúde, ACM Neto voltou a se comprometer com o impedimento de aumentos no valor de contribuição do servidor público ao Plano de Saúde dos Servidores Públicos Estaduais da Bahia (Planserv). Citou ainda suas propostas para proporcionar melhorias na chamada fila da regulação.

"Quero, nesse momento, me dirigir a vocês que acompanharam essa entrevista, fazendo uma pergunta: 'Quem tem mais chance de resolver os problemas da Bahia? Um governador que prometeu, há quatro anos atrás, zerar a fila da regulação, enfrentar o crime, melhorar a qualidade da educação e fazer a Bahia crescer, e nada disso aconteceu, ou eu, que fui [por] oito anos considerado o melhor prefeito das capitais brasileiras, que saí com mais de 80% de aprovação, que rodei todo esse estado, que tenho um amor enorme pela Bahia?'. Eu quero fazer história, eu quero permitir que a Bahia tenha o melhor governo de todo o Brasil. Eu garanto: 'Vocês não vão se decepcionar comigo'. Jerônimo já teve a chance dele. Eu, agora, peço a sua chance. Então, dia 4 de outubro, por favor, confia na gente, votem 44 e vamos mudar a Bahia", disse.

articles.title: SIR on duty, just not for studies: Full academic year may be at risk
articles.summary: Election duty leaves Delhi govt teachers juggling classes and Special Intensive Revision voter verification till Dec, raising fears of disrupted teaching and exams.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: With teachers juggling classrooms and election work for months, educators fear their continuing deployment could end up taking a toll on an entire academic year in some govt schools.What began as a time-bound exercise has stretched through crucial months of teaching, and with SIR-related work expected to continue till Dec, school heads say managing regular classes, examinations and evaluation alongside field duties is becoming increasingly difficult.“The entire academic year is getting affected,” said a govt school principal. “If teachers continue with this work till Dec and Census-related work begins after that, when the entire staff may again be involved, then when will teaching happen?”A large number of teachers serving as booth-level officers (BLOs) are balancing their regular school responsibilities with work related to Election Commission’s Special Intensive Revision (SIR).Their duties have expanded further following a change in the verification process for voters who could not be traced or whose records showed discrepancies. BLOs will now have to visit such voters at their homes, collect the required documents and upload them for scrutiny by the electoral registration officer, rather than requiring these cases to be resolved through in-person hearings.According to the head of a school in northwest Delhi, teachers deployed for the exercise are now expected to remain engaged till Dec, although the work had initially been expected to conclude around Oct. He added that while officially the directions state that work has to be done “beyond school hours”, it was impossible to manage along with regular classes.“In my school, I have given them relaxation for half the day. They remain in school till around 11am and we schedule their periods accordingly. After that, they leave for this work,” he said. But elsewhere, he added, teachers are expected to remain in school until 1pm or 2pm before beginning field visits.“A teacher works in school till 11am, noon or even 2pm, then goes into the field and works there till 6pm or 7pm. After that, there is uploading work at night. They are doing this on Saturdays and Sundays as well,” the principal said, adding that the loss of even one teacher can be especially difficult at the senior secondary level, where a school may have only one person teaching a specialised subject.Another school head said 34 teachers from his school had earlier spent more than 40 days on full-time BLO duty. Even when teachers are asked to keep election work outside school hours, that boundary does not always hold. “They come to us at noon or 1pm and say they have to go to the field,” he said. “It is at the cost of studies.”School heads are also being drawn into the exercise. The northwest Delhi principal said 53 principals in his zone had recently been assigned SIR-related duties after a notification at the end of Sept.Meanwhile, teachers remain answerable both to their schools and to election officials. articles.title: Florida officials have cleared the way for a $100 million-plus surf park where developers plan a 35-acre attraction with a six-acre artificial wave lagoon and half-mile beach miles from the ocean
articles.summary: A major new attraction is moving forward in Wesley Chapel, Florida, bringing the possibility of ocean-style surfing to a community located miles from the
articles.body: A major new attraction is moving forward in Wesley Chapel, Florida, bringing the possibility of ocean-style surfing to a community located miles from the coast. According to the Pasco County Community Website, Pasco County commissioners voted 3-0 in September to approve a comprehensive plan amendment and rezoning connected to the Two Rivers development. The approval clears an important land-use hurdle for Peak Surf Park, a proposed $100 million-plus project expected to include a 35-acre destination, a six-acre artificial wave lagoon and a half-mile sandy beach. Developers are targeting a late 2027 opening, although additional permits and construction milestones still need to be completed. Read on to know more here:A surf park in Wesley ChapelPeak Surf Park is planned along State Road 56 near U.S. 301, on the eastern side of the large Two Rivers development closest to Zephyrhills. Although the attraction would be far from the Gulf of Mexico, its central feature is designed to create the feeling of surfing at the beach. Visitors would enter a large artificial lagoon where mechanical equipment would generate waves for people with different levels of experience.The project would use Surf Lakes technology, developed in Australia. At the centre of the lagoon, a large plunger would move up and down to push waves outward in several directions at the same time. This design is intended to create different surf breaks around the lagoon, allowing beginners and experienced surfers to use the same facility during a session.Project details reviewed during the county approval process indicate that the lagoon could accommodate as many as 200 surfers per hour. Each surfer is expected to catch about 10 waves per session. That would give visitors more opportunities to practise than they might find at a crowded natural beach, where wave conditions can change quickly and access is often limited.More than a wave poolThe proposed attraction would be designed as a complete entertainment and lifestyle destination rather than a facility focused only on surfing. Plans call for a half-mile sandy beach around the lagoon, along with restaurants, bars, retail shops, fitness facilities and wellness spaces. An outdoor venue for concerts and other events is also included in the broader concept.The lagoon alone would require roughly eight million gallons of water. According to the project information, the water would be pumped into the facility over a period of two to three weeks. That detail has become one of the most closely watched parts of the proposal, especially because Pasco County faced water-use restrictions during an extreme water shortage earlier this year.Developer Tony Miller, a longtime Tampa-area surfer, has reportedly spent about two years working to secure the site and move the concept through the approval process. The project is being promoted as a way to bring consistent surfing conditions to the Tampa Bay region, which has warm weather and a large population but no dependable natural surf.Concerns over water and growthThe approval was not without opposition. During public meetings, residents raised concerns about water consumption, flooding, traffic, wildlife habitat and the loss of open land. More than a dozen people spoke against aspects of the proposal at a July planning hearing, questioning whether the surf park and the wider Two Rivers expansion could place too much pressure on local roads and utilities.The surf park is part of a much larger development plan covering 3,405 acres along State Road 56 between Morris Bridge Road and Gall Boulevard. Earlier versions of the plan included thousands of homes, apartments, townhomes and villas, as well as a hotel, an assisted living facility and approximately 1.3 million square feet of retail space.That scale means the future attraction cannot be viewed separately from the wider growth of the area. A popular surf park could bring visitors, jobs and new businesses, but it could also contribute to traffic and increase demand for water and public services. How those pressures are managed will likely remain a major issue as the project moves through later stages.Housing linked to the projectCounty commissioners attached a condition to the approval that connects a portion of the proposed housing to the surf park’s progress. Under the condition, the developer may add up to 240 garden-style apartments, but construction on those units cannot begin until Peak Surf Park receives its certificate of occupancy or three years have passed after the land-use amendment takes effect, whichever comes first.The condition gives the county a way to tie residential development to the delivery of the promised attraction. In practical terms, the project must reach a defined stage before the developer can move ahead with that part of the housing plan. Supporters may view the requirement as a safeguard, while opponents may argue that it does not address all of the broader infrastructure concerns linked to the Two Rivers buildout.Technology still facing a major testAlthough Surf Lakes has operated its wave-generating system at a lake in Yeppoon, Queensland, the technology has not yet been used at a fully operational commercial surf park where customers pay to ride. That makes the Wesley Chapel proposal particularly significant for the company and the emerging surf-park industry.Peak Surf Park could become one of the first paying venues to rely on the system. The success of the attraction will depend not only on the quality and consistency of the waves, but also on construction costs, safety, operating expenses and whether visitors are willing to pay for repeated sessions.County approval establishes the land-use framework, but it does not mean construction has begun. Developers still need to complete additional permitting and design work before breaking ground. The late 2027 opening target remains possible, although the schedule could change depending on approvals, financing, construction progress and the performance of the wave technology.If completed as planned, Peak Surf Park would give residents and visitors a place to surf without travelling to the ocean. It could become a distinctive new destination for Wesley Chapel and the wider Tampa Bay region, while also testing whether artificial wave attractions can succeed in rapidly growing communities far from the coast.You use AI every day. articles.title: Apple Pay launches in India; here's how to set it up and where you can use it
articles.summary: Apple has officially launched Apple Pay in India.
articles.body: Apple has officially launched Apple Pay in India. With this launch the company brings its secure and seamless payment system to iPhone, iPad and Apple Watch users, with Mac support coming soon. Apple Pay roll out in the country will enable users to pay in stores, apps, and on the web without typing PINs and OTPs marking a significant milestone in India’s fast-growing digital payments ecosystem. At launch, Apple Pay supports Axis Bank-issued Visa and Mastercard credit cards, enabling payments at thousands of merchants across India and anywhere NFC transactions are accepted globally.Apple also emphasised that privacy remains central to how Apple Pay functions. When a card is added, the actual card number is never stored on the device or Apple's servers, nor shared with merchants during a transaction. Instead, the system assigns a unique Device Account Number, which is encrypted and stored securely within the device's Secure Element — a certified, industry-standard chip built specifically to protect payment information.Apple Pay launched in India: How it works, and who can use itPresently, Apple Pay is exclusively available to customers holding Axis Bank-issued Visa and Mastercard credit cards, letting them add those cards to Apple Pay and use them at thousands of in-store and online merchants across India, as well as anywhere that accepts NFC transactions.Jennifer Bailey, Apple's vice president of Apple Pay and Apple Wallet, framed the launch as a natural fit for India's fast-growing digital economy, pointing to the country's dynamic, digitally savvy population that's increasingly embracing cashless payments while expecting strong security and privacy standards. She described Apple Pay's core value proposition as making everyday card payments easy, secure, and private — from a simple tap in stores without needing a separate app, PIN, or OTP, to checking out online without repeatedly re-entering payment details.How to set up and use Apple PayApple Pay is easy to set up. Customers can add a card directly to Apple Wallet via the latest version of the Axis Bank app. Alternatively, simply open the Wallet app on iPhone, tap the plus sign, and follow the steps to add an eligible card. Once a user adds a card to their Apple device, they can start using Apple Pay right away.Using Apple Pay in stores is seamless and easy. Simply double-click the side button or Home button; authenticate using Face ID, Touch ID, or a device passcode if prompted; and hold the top of the iPhone or display of the Apple Watch near the contactless reader to pay. When using Apple Pay, users will continue to earn the rewards and benefits offered by their cards.Where you can use itAt launch, Apple Pay will be accepted at millions of merchants across India, including Apple Store locations, Blinkit, Chaayos, Comet, Croma, Interflora, Ixigo, Le15 Patisserie, Reliance brands, Tata 1mg, and Zomato, among others. Apple has also partnered with several payment service providers, including Cashfree, JusPay, Mswipe, Paytm, PayU, Pine Labs, Razorpay, and Worldline, to extend Apple Pay's reach across their respective merchant networks, with more merchants and apps expected to be added over time.Globally, Apple Pay is now available in more than 90 countries and regions, working with over 11,000 bank and network partners worldwide — making India one of the more prominent recent additions to that global rollout.You use AI every day. articles.title: Google CEO Sundar Pichai 'agrees' to the call that technology companies need to innovate responsibly; says: As I shared today ...
articles.summary: Google CEO Sundar Pichai has joined the US President Donald Trump, Senate leaders, and other tech executives in signing the White House Accord on Super
articles.body: Google CEO Sundar Pichai has joined the US President Donald Trump, Senate leaders, and other tech executives in signing the White House Accord on Super Intelligence, a landmark agreement aimed at ensuring safe and responsible development of advanced AI systems. The accord, alongside a Joint Commitment on Frontier Responsibilities, sets out tangible steps for companies to adopt safeguards while continuing to deliver economic and scientific benefits. Pichai revealed that Google has invested hundreds of billions of dollars in the past two years across its AI stack, with more spending planned. He emphasized that the company is focused on building products that deliver real value for people and businesses, while also investing in local communities and strengthening public trust in technology.What Google CEO Sundar Pichai saidIn a post on X, Pichai described the meeting as an important conversation, confirming that Google had signed what he called the White House Accord on Super Intelligence. “Great to meet today with @POTUS, @JDVance, @SpeakerJohnsonand Administration + tech leaders. Important conversation and we signed today the White House Accord on Super Intelligence.As I shared today, Google has invested hundreds of billions in the last two years alone, with more to come, across the entire stack, to deliver benefits for America and the world. We’re working to build products that deliver real value for people and businesses, invest in local communities, and build trust in the technology.Industry also has to innovate responsibly. Google’s focused on building the right way, with appropriate testing, evaluations, red-teaming, and other safeguards against misuse and misalignment – and releasing models or products only after they’ve been thoroughly reviewed.We are committed to working with other industry leaders to establish norms and build public confidence. The White House Accord and the Joint Commitment on Frontier Responsibilities signed today is a solid basis for moving forward - it contains real tangible steps to promote safe development, while delivering the economic and scientific benefits of this technology,” wrote Pichai in a post on X.What the accord actually saysThe full agreement is titled "The White House Accord on Superintelligence: Joint Commitment on Frontier SI Responsibilities." Beyond Pichai, it was signed by Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, OpenAI President Greg Brockman, xAI founder Elon Musk, and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, alongside Trump himself.The one-page document lays out what's being described as a four-layer framework of controls and audits for frontier AI systems. The first layer requires companies to build robust internal processes to monitor their models during both training and deployment, ensuring systems behave as intended and that problems are identified and resolved quickly. Subsequent layers call for internal verification, partnerships with independent external auditors to assess whether safety controls are functioning as intended, and board-level oversight of the entire process.Voluntary, not legally bindingDespite its formal tone, House Speaker Mike Johnson was clear that the accord is entirely voluntary, and Trump himself described it as "morally" binding rather than legally enforceable, emphasizing that the industry will largely be left to police itself. At the signing event, Trump likened the document to a kind of constitution for AI governance, while Musk described the substance of the commitment as involving joint monitoring, special board committees, and companies essentially reviewing each other's safety practices.Zuckerberg struck a similarly measured tone afterward, calling the accord a reasonable starting point — one the broader industry could plausibly coalesce around going forward, rather than a finished framework.You use AI every day. articles.summary: MUMBAI: A BMC employee was killed and two others injured after a speeding car allegedly rammed into two scooters on CD Road in Khar West on Monday, with
articles.body: MUMBAI: A BMC employee was killed and two others injured after a speeding car allegedly rammed into two scooters on CD Road in Khar West on Monday, with CCTV footage capturing the crash.Police have registered an FIR against retired honorary Brigadier and former Rajapur MP Sudhir Sawant in connection with the incident.The CCTV footage shows the car hitting the scooters on the busy road, after which Iyappan Harijan, 41, was trapped underneath the vehicle. Bystanders lifted the car and pulled him out before he and his wife Nancy, 37, were taken to Bhabha Hospital in an autorickshaw.Harijan suffered severe injuries and repeatedly lost consciousness while being taken to hospital. He later died from blood loss.Nancy, who was riding pillion, suffered bruises on her left hand and other parts of her body. Another scooter rider, Rahul Ghanekar, suffered a fractured hand.Recalling the crash, Nancy said she saw her husband trapped beneath the car, with only his leg visible. People gathered at the spot and lifted the vehicle to pull him out. She said Harijan initially managed to sit up but had injuries to his head, face and other parts of his body.Khar police on Tuesday registered an FIR against Sawant, 71, under relevant Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita sections for causing death by negligence and rash and dangerous driving.Police said further action would be taken after Sawant is discharged from hospital. He was undergoing treatment after his blood pressure rose following the accident.According to Nancy’s complaint, the couple had left their home in Santacruz West around 4.15pm to shop in Bandra for an event at their home when the car allegedly hit their scooter from behind.Harijan had worked with MTNL for 16 years before joining BMC’s cleaning services department about a month ago. articles.summary: BHOPAL: A retired IAS officer, Rakesh Agrawal, was allegedly found dead with his throat slit at his residence behind Panghat Colony in Suraj Nagar in
articles.body: BHOPAL: A retired IAS officer, Rakesh Agrawal, was allegedly found dead with his throat slit at his residence behind Panghat Colony in Suraj Nagar in Ratibad early Wednesday morning.A caretaker, who had reportedly been hired through an agency just four days ago, was found missing from the house.Police suspect the caretaker may have fled after the incident. His belongings, except for a pair of clothes, were reportedly missing from the premises. He is said to be from Punjab.According to preliminary information, Agrawal and his wife slept in separate rooms. Around 4am, his wife woke up and found the door of her room latched from outside.She called another caretaker, Amar, who stayed in the servant quarters. Amar opened the door, following which they checked Agrawal's room and found that it too had been latched from outside.When the door was opened, Agrawal was found lying dead inside. His throat had allegedly been slit.Police were also informed after LPG cylinders in the kitchen were found leaking, raising suspicion that an attempt may have been made to cause an explosion at the house.Teams from Ratibad police station, along with senior police officers and forensic experts, reached the spot and began investigating the circumstances surrounding the death. The forensic team examined the scene and collected evidence.Senior IAS officers also reached the residence after learning about the incident.
